overall: Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by under-specifying the executive session topic, failing to follow executive session procedures, and keeping inaccurate minutes; minute fixes were adequate but other remedial steps were not.

allegations.summary: Notice for the Sept. 5, 2012 meeting listed an executive session topic without naming the union being negotiated with.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to list a topic with sufficient specificity on its meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Motion to enter executive session was insufficient, the chair did not announce the bargaining-unit purpose in open session, and did not state whether the body would reconvene.
allegations.key_passage: Likewise, this detail about the purpose for the executive session should have been included in Chairman Steinberg's announcement in open session.

allegations.summary: Meeting minutes for the Sept. 5, 2012 meeting did not accurately reflect the executive session motion language.
allegations.key_passage: by failing to create accurate meeting minutes

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
